source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Use "dd" command to fill files in all avaliable storages until the spaces are full.
2. Check the MD5 of files.
3. Reboot system.
4. After reboot, check the MD5 of files.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The spaces should be filled with files without errors.
2. After reboot, the MD5 of files should be correct.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Fill a user-selected partition only to a user-selected near-full percentage and run a write check.
deepseek_columns.risk: Near-full affects operation; use dedicated target.

original_test_intent: Fill filesystems on every approved dedicated SSD storage target to the owner-defined source-equivalent full boundary, prove all generated files retain identical checksums across a controlled reboot and verify filesystem, device and system health.
original_method: Allowlist each dedicated non-system mount and reserve/recovery boundary, generate deterministic files with dd while recording sizes and digests, establish the defined full condition, compute complete MD5 manifests, reboot once, remount and verify every manifest, then collect capacity, health, filesystem and log evidence before approved cleanup.
manual_activity: An authorized user supplies and approves exact targets, the meaning of full, reboot and cleanup, and later issues the verdict. These inputs do not make the file generation, checksums, reboot, remount verification and evidence collection non-automatable.
required_inputs: Every target's mount, filesystem, device/serial and proof it is dedicated, non-system and safe to fill
Exact full boundary, expected ENOSPC handling or reserved free-space floor for services
dd file naming/size/count, MD5 manifest scope, fsync/sync requirements and retention
Stable power, maintenance/reboot approval, console/OOB and boot recovery
Health/log monitoring, abort thresholds and exact cleanup/free-space restoration procedure
safety_requirements: Never fill an OS/root, boot, mounted production, in-use, protected or ambiguous filesystem; use an immutable allowlist.
Maintain the approved reserve needed for logging, reboot and recovery unless the owner explicitly defines safe true-full behavior on an isolated target.
Stop on wrong target, unsafe free space, I/O/filesystem/media/thermal errors, service instability or failed boot/remount.
Preserve the first error and manifests; do not auto-retry, delete arbitrary files or clean up beyond the exact generated-file list.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target identities, full/reserve semantics, file/checksum and cleanup plan; capture storage/health/log baseline.
After approval, generate only named test files, record capacity and MD5 manifest, sync, perform one controlled reboot and verify complete post-reboot digests.
Collect health/log/cleanup evidence and report exact target coverage and Tool Result without declaring PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Resolve the full-versus-no-error ambiguity and approve every target, reserve, reboot and cleanup boundary.
Review integrity and health evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its near-full single-target suggestion is safer but not source-equivalent and omits checksum/reboot coverage. dd/fallocate must not be run until target paths and bounds are exact; fallocate may not exercise data writes equivalently to dd.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a manifest-driven dd file-generation workflow on exact dedicated mounts, compute complete pre/post MD5 manifests, sync and verify after one controlled reboot; cleanup only generated paths.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: dd file fill on all approved available storages, MD5 before/after reboot and 15/8-minute fields are preserved; any near-full override is reported explicitly.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create uniquely named deterministic test files with byte totals and digests, continuously record free space and health, persist the manifest outside targets, verify after reboot and remove only manifest-owned files under approval.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS/kernel, filesystem, dd/coreutils, checksum utility, storage firmware and controller versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project filesystem/fullness and reboot/cleanup specification must define the safe boundary; no generic percentage is treated as source-equivalent.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds safe target/reserve and exact artifact ownership while retaining fill and checksum/reboot semantics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; all approved targets and complete pre/post checksums remain required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: True ENOSPC may impair logging/services and the terminal dd behavior must be explicitly interpreted.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve near-full rather than true-full or a subset of storage. The report must state the percentage/reserve and target subset and may claim only that project plan, not the master all-storage/full requirement.
expected_evidence: Per-target mount/device/serial/filesystem/usage allowlist, baseline capacity/health and authorization
Resolved full/reserve/ENOSPC rule, exact generated-file manifest and complete pre-reboot MD5 values
Fill transcript, free-space/error timeline, sync and controlled reboot/remount evidence
Complete post-reboot MD5 comparison, health/logs, approved cleanup/free-space restoration, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure says fill until spaces are full, which normally terminates with ENOSPC or requires a reserved boundary, while the criterion requires filling 'without errors.' The owner must define whether expected terminal ENOSPC is acceptable or how full is reached without it; this cannot be silently changed to near-full.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The data-integrity stress intent is clear. Targets/fullness/cleanup are project inputs and the recorded conflict can be resolved without creating a permanent blocker; the execution core is fully automatable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its unreported near-full coverage reduction and restores MD5/reboot verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains target, cleanup and approval gates while advancing capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE under V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records the true-full/no-error conflict and adds manifest-owned cleanup plus project-override claim boundaries.

review_improvement: Prevents system-volume exhaustion and arbitrary deletion while preserving all-target fullness and reboot integrity instead of quietly weakening the test.
independent_technical_reasoning: All core operations are deterministic filesystem actions and electronic reboot/evidence steps; exact targets and authorization are inputs, not manual capability limits. The only unresolved source issue is how 'full without errors' treats ENOSPC, so the case is FULLY AUTOMATABLE with a recorded SOURCE_CONFLICT, not BLOCKED.
